transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, honestly... what really made me come in is this feeling I can't shake. I'm a buyer for retail, and lately, I just know that people at work—and even some of the vendors—are tracking my buys. It feels like they're intentionally messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps showing me reports trying to prove that's not happening, but... I just can't stop thinking they're all in on it.
Have you been hearing voices or sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

Yeah, actually, I have. Um, sometimes when I'm in the stockroom, or if I'm driving back from a vendor meeting, I'll hear a man's voice. It sounds like it's coming from right behind me. He'll say things like, 'Move faster, Scott,' or he'll just start laughing at my picks. But whenever I turn around to check... nobody's there.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energetic, or revved up for days at a time?

Yeah, there are definitely times like that. When I get really keyed up, I just... I can't handle doing only one task at a time. I end up doing a bunch of things all at once. 

Like, I'll be emailing three different vendors, putting together a whole new buy plan, and reorganizing the product samples all at the same time. And I'll just be pacing around the office while I do it, because it feels like if I actually stop moving, I'll just completely lose the thread of everything I'm working on.
Have the voice and the feeling that people are tracking you ever happened during a time when you were not feeling especially high or revved up?

Yeah, they actually have. Um... there was a calmer stretch a little while ago. I was sleeping more normally, and I definitely didn't feel like I was running the whole market or anything like that. But even then... for a few weeks, I still completely believed people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom.
During those keyed-up periods, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah, definitely. Um, there have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe three or four hours a night. But I wake up feeling completely wired and ready to go. When I'm like that, I just think lying in bed is a waste of time, honestly. It just feels like time I could use to actually make moves and get things done.
During those wired, high-energy periods, did you feel unusually powerful or important?

Yeah, I do. I get this feeling like... like I'm the most important person in the room. I start believing I can spot the next big trend before anyone else in L.A. catches on. Like the whole sneaker market is basically just waiting on my decisions to see what to do next. Which, you know, doesn't really make sense since I'm still just one of the junior buyers, but in the moment, I feel like I'm running the whole show.
Have the voice and the belief that people were tracking your buys been going on for more than a month altogether?
Yeah, definitely more than a month. I'd say the feeling that people are tracking me, and hearing that voice... it's been going on for about ten months now altogether.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had any periods where I felt down or depressed like that, definitely not for two weeks straight. It's mostly just been the wired feeling or dealing with the voice and the tracking stuff.
Over the time these problems have been going on, have the wired, high-energy periods made up most of the illness?

Yeah, I'd say so. Looking back on it, most of the time since this all started has been taken up by those wired stretches. Like, the times where I was just overworking, feeling super overconfident, and just... really hard to slow down. There were some shorter, calmer periods in between, but the high-energy stuff definitely made up the majority of it.
